title: I Before E
kidRule: When I and E team up to say 'ee', the I usually comes first, like in BELIEVE. Right after the letter C they flip to E-I, like in CEILING. A few rebels break the rule, like WEIRD!
hint: Listen for the 'ee' sound. Two vowels team up to make it, and their order matters! Peek at the letter that comes just before them.
reminder: For the 'ee' sound, it is I before E, except right after C, where it flips to E-I.

check.question: Why does the I come before the E in BELIEVE?
check.correctAnswer: Because I usually comes before E, unless they come right after the letter C!
distractors: Because vowels always go in ABC order
Because E always has to be the last vowel in a word

words.sent: I believe you can do it if you try.
words.story: A few hundred years ago, many people in Europe believed that tomatoes were poisonous and would not eat them!
words.card: I do not *believe* the dragon's *lie* that broccoli is candy!

words.sent: A balloon floated up to the ceiling.
words.story: The artist Michelangelo spent about four years painting the ceiling of one famous chapel, standing on a tall wooden platform!
words.card: There is a pancake stuck *in* the kitchen *ceiling*!

words.sent: The knight held up his shield to block the arrow.
words.story: Earth has an invisible shield! Its magnetic field protects us from tiny, speedy bits that fly out of the Sun.
words.card: The *eld*est knight used his *shield* as a sled on the snowy hill!

words.sent: My niece is learning to ride a bike.
words.story: Some people call their nieces and nephews their 'niblings', a word made up to match 'siblings'!
words.card: My *niece* baked a p*ie* as big as a trampoline!

words.card: What a *relief* to *lie* down after chasing the runaway pancake!

words.def: To get something that is given or sent to you.

words.story: Golden retrievers got their name because they were first raised in Scotland to fetch things from land and water!
words.card: My dog *trie*d to *retrieve* the moon from a puddle!

words.sent: Dad kept the receipt in case the shoes did not fit.
words.story: Some of the oldest writing ever found, on clay tablets thousands of years old, is a kind of receipt for things like grain and sheep!
words.card: The monkey framed the *receipt* from its *rec*ord-breaking banana shopping trip!
